 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
Present:
The Hon'ble Justice Ananya Bandyopadhyay

 Bhabani Biswas & Ors.
 -Vs-
 National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.
For the Appellants/claimants : Mr. Muktakesh Das

Ms. Jaita Ghosh Heard on : 08.08.2024 Judgment on : 08.08.2024

1. The Learned Advocates for the appellants/claimants as well as the
respondents/insurance company are present.

2. The instant appeal has been filed against the judgment dated 18th September, 2017
passed by the M.A.C. Tribunal - cum -
Additional District & Sessions Judge, Ftc-I, Krishnanagar, Nadia in Mac Case No.86 of 2016 under
Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

The compensation award in the instant claim case to the extent of Rs.2,01,500/- is disputed in view of the Notification dated 22nd May, 2018 issued by the appropriate authority through Gazette publication and also the observation of this Court in Urmila Halder v. 4.

sentences.text:
The claimants had filed an application under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 whereby the aforesaid Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,01,500/- along with interest at the rate of 8%
per annum from the date of filing of the aforesaid claim application till the realization of the entire amount.

The notification dated 22.05.2018, inter alia, stated as follows:

sentences.text: Compensation payable in case of Death shall be five lakh rupees".
5. The occurrence of the accident, the veracity of the driving licence, route permit, etc. and other ancillary issues are not in dispute.

However, in view of the aforesaid notification and the decisions of the Hon'ble High Court at Calcutta as well as the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Special Leave Petition2,
the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.5,00,000/-.

6. The impugned judgment passed by the aforesaid tribunal is modified to the extent of Rs.2,98,500/- (Rs.5,00,000- Rs.2,01,500/-) along with interest to be paid at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of filing of the application till the date of its actual realization.

The Learned Advocate for the 2019(2)TAC 143 Special Leave Petition (Civil) No. 6260 of 2019 appellants/claimants submitted to have received the compensation of Rs. 2,01,500/-.
7.

The Learned Advocate for the respondent/insurance company is to deposit the balance sum of Rs.
2,98,500/- along with 6 % per cent interest per annum from the date of filing of the claim application before the office of the learned Registrar General, High Court Calcutta within eight weeks from the date of passing of this order.

8. On receipt of the said amount, the office of the Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta shall encash the said cheque and thereafter disburse the same to the present appellants/claimants in equal proportion as mentioned in the impugned judgment passed by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge, FTC-I, Krishnanagar, Nadia in Motor Accident Claims Case No.86 of 2016 on proof of proper identification of the appellants/claimants subject to payment of ad valorem Courts fees.
